author: Hoo, C. S.
document_title: Some fuzzy concepts of BCI, BCK and MV-algebras
spelling: Hoo, C. S.; Hoo, Cheong-Seng; Hoo, Cheong S.
review_text:
The author systematizes some concepts and results of his previous works [Fuzzy Sets Syst. 62, No. 1, 111-114 (1994; Zbl 0826.06011); ibid. 66, No. 3, 315-327 (1994; Zbl 0844.06007); ibid. 72, No. 2, 197-204 (1995; Zbl 0844.06008)] in the context of BCI-algebras. In particular, if \(Z\) is an MV-algebra, then he shows that a fuzzy ideal \(
u\) of \(Z\) is fuzzy implicative, prime, essential, weakly essential and maximal iff the MV-ideal \(Z_{
u} = \{x \in Z : 
u(x) = 
u(0)\}\) has the respective non-fuzzy property. Moreover, if \(X\) is a quasi-commutative BCI-algebra, the author proves a one-to-one correspondence between the set of the fuzzy closed ideals of \(X\) and the set of the fuzzy congruences of \(X\).

author: Novák, Vilém
document_title: Open theories, consistency and related results in fuzzy logic
spelling: Novák, Vilém; Novák, V.; Novak, Vilem; Novák, Vilem; Vilem, Novak; Novak, V.
review_text: In order to set the background for the resolution method development and application in fuzzy logic, the author considers a generalization of Łukasiewicz first-order logic having many important properties. Namely, it is shown that for this logic the corresponding generalizations of the deduction and completeness theorem hold. In this way a syntactical reasoning on truth values is provided, establishing a formal tool for the modeling of the vagueness phenomenon. As the crucial step approaching resolution, an analogue to the Herbrand theorem is proved as well, providing a good formal basis for resolution in the context of fuzzy logic.

author: Sato, Takeshi
document_title: The flat holomorphic conformal structure on the Horrocks-Mumford orbifold
review_text: The authors construct explicitly the flat conformal structure on \(\mathbb{P} (\Gamma {\mathcal F}_{HM})\) that is the pullback of the flat conformal structure on \({\mathcal A}_{1,5}\). Here \({\mathcal F}_{HM}\) is the Horrocks- Mumford vector bundle on \(\mathbb{P}^ 4\) and \(\Gamma {\mathcal F}_{HM}\) is the space of its sections. Since the vanishing locus of sections of \({\mathcal F}_{HM}\) are Abelian surfaces, there is a rational map from \(\mathbb{P} (\Gamma {\mathcal F}_{HM})\) to \({\mathcal A}_{1,5}\), the moduli space of Abelian surfaces with (1,5)-polarization and level 5-structure. It has a canonical flat conformal structure since \({\mathcal A}_{1,5}\) is a quotient of a Siegel upper half plane. The explicit form of its pull back on \(\mathbb{P} (\Gamma {\mathcal F}_{HM})\) is given in the paper under review.
